chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a question, and he answered me. Then a man came and asked him the same question, and he answered him differently from how he had answered me. Then another man came and he answered him differently from how he had answered me and how he had answered my companion. When the two men left, I said: 'O son of the Messenger of God! Two men from the people of Iraq, from your Shia, came asking, and you answered each of the two with something other than what you answered his companion.' He said: 'O Zurara! This is better for us and more lasting for us and for you. And if you all were to gather upon one matter, the people would confirm your words against us, and it would be less for our survival and yours.'

He (the narrator) said: Then I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Your Shia — if you were to command them onto spears or into fire, they would march forward, yet they come out from your presence differing.' He said: So he answered me with the like of his father's answer.

key_terms.بخلاف: Contrary to, differently from — denoting intentional divergence in rulings
key_terms.بقاء: Survival, preservation — referring to the physical safety of both the Imams and the Shia community
key_terms.صدَّقكم الناس علينا: The people would confirm your words against us — meaning opponents would use a unified Shia position as evidence to persecute the Imams
key_terms.مختلفين: Differing, in disagreement — describing the apparent state of Shia when leaving the Imam's presence

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir give different answers to different people about the same question?
ai.summary: Zurara ibn A'yan narrates a remarkable exchange with Imam al-Baqir (AS) and later with Imam al-Sadiq (AS). Zurara was puzzled when the Imam gave different answers to the same question to different questioners. Imam al-Baqir explained that this intentional variation (taqiyya-based dispersion of rulings) was a protective measure: if the community were to unanimously agree on a single answer, it would expose the Imams to danger from those who would 'confirm' (i.e., report and use) those teachings against them. The Imam's response underscored that the deliberate diversity of hadith transmission was a divinely sanctioned strategy for the preservation of both the Imams and their followers during a period of 'Abbasid suppression. Imam al-Sadiq's identical response to the same complaint confirmed this as a consistent Imamic position.
word_analysis: they would believe you/confirm your words

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Zurara Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> a question, so he<sup>asws</sup> answered me.

Then a man came over, so he asked him<sup>asws</sup> about it, so he<sup>asws</sup> answered differently to what he<sup>asws</sup> had answered me. Then another man came over, so he<sup>asws</sup> answered him differently to what he<sup>asws</sup> had answered me and to what he<sup>asws</sup> had answered my companion.
So when the two men went out, I said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Two men from the people of Al-Iraq, from your<sup>asws</sup> Shias came over asking, so you<sup>asws</sup> answered one of the two with other than what you<sup>asws</sup> answered his companion’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Zurara! This is better for us<sup>asws</sup> and more remaining for us<sup>asws</sup> and for you all. And if they were all to gather upon one matter, the people would (start) believe upon us<sup>asws</sup>. But, it would be less for our<sup>asws</sup> preservation and your preservation’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Your<sup>asws</sup> Shia, if you<sup>asws</sup> were to carry them upon the arrows or upon the fire, they would be walking (upon these), and they are (now) coming out from your<sup>asws</sup> presence, differing’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> answered me with similar to the answer of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Al-Thaqafi‘laba ibn Maymun from Zurara ibn ‘A‘yan who has said the following.

“I asked Imam abu Ja‘far (a.s.) a question and he answered me. Then an other man came and asked the same question but the Imam gave a different answer. Then a third man came and asked the same question but the Imam gave him an answer that was different from both of the previous answers. When the other two men left I asked the Imam (a.s.), “Two of your followers from Iraq asked you the same question, how is it that you gave each one a different answer? The Imam replied, “O Zurarah, it is better for us and it gives all of us more time. If you all would say the same thing, people will know that you speak the truth from us and this will leave all of us with less time.

Zurarah has said, “I then asked Imam abu ‘Abdallah, ‘Your follows would walk on spears and fire if you would ask them but they come out of your presence with different answers for the same question and the same answer as his father had given.”
